configuration_reports.label: yes
controls_available: A 9x7 course has one ordered relay and a dock; the generated route is constrained to 7-12 moves.

A visible pressure pad moves with a 4800 ms sinusoidal period, x amplitude 155-175 milli, y amplitude 95-115 milli, and a 270x310 milli hit ellipse; samples are required every 140 ms, with a 520 ms maximum gap and 460 ms outside grace.
Full input is a primary-pointer press held on the pressure pad with pointer movement to track it, plus WASD or arrow-key presses for course movement; the continuous hold must last at least 3000 ms.
autonomous_processes: While live task time runs, requestAnimationFrame repeatedly moves the visible pressure pad along its sinusoidal x/y trajectory.

During a full hold, the same loop checks the last pointer position, emits pressure samples when it is inside the moving hit ellipse, updates the continuity display, and resets the route after the configured outside grace if tracking is lost.
The vehicle, relay progress, and route position do not advance autonomously; they change only after accepted keyboard movement.
grouped_control_modes: full:pointer_tracking — every held-pointer start, tracking move/sample, and release/reset occurrence across seeds and attempts
full:keyboard — every WASD or arrow-key course movement while the pointer hold is active

clause_i.reason: For D=full:pointer_tracking, the generator randomizes the pressure period, phase, and amplitudes. Histories with the same prior actions and task times can therefore show different current trajectories, so no action-only q can choose the delayed pointer target for every history.

clause_ii.reason: The five chronological frames in the configured 500 ms observation window visibly show the pad's recent position and direction. A bounded-window g can use that trajectory, together with the action history, to place the held pointer at the predicted pad location 200 ms later.

clause_iii.reason: Using the same moving-pad process, choose a held pointer position just inside the leading edge of the hit ellipse. A pointer-tracking action at that visible location is useful immediately, but for some tau<200 ms the pad moves past it and the action loses its pressure-sampling advantage. Success remains possible because the 200 ms horizon is below this level's 460 ms outside grace and the route can be recovered.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: The visible pressure pad continuously follows the sinusoidal trajectory. Its recent motion is the evidence needed to predict the delayed full pointer target, and the same motion makes a fixed pointer location less effective during the 200 ms witness horizon.

pre_run.reason: Every generated course needs at least seven accepted moves. Full mode accepts those moves only as outcome-affecting keyboard events while a continuous pointer hold is active, and it also needs continuing pointer tracking, so no instance can complete its outcome phase without further outcome-affecting actions.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 sets the 9x7 one-relay course, pressure tolerances and sampling/grace values, and the 500 ms/5-frame observation settings.
The configured difficulty parameters generate alternating relay gaps, a route, and randomized period, phase, amplitudes, hit tolerances, and sampling thresholds.
The pad position is a time-dependent sine trajectory; full mode starts a pointer-tracking hold, updates it from pointermove, samples it, and resets when it leaves too long.
requestAnimationFrame callbacks run with the virtual task clock while live and remain queued while paused.
The grader binds full mode to pointer_tracking plus keyboard, requires continuous pressure samples and movement during one hold, and enforces the minimum hold and sampling gaps.
The full solver holds the pointer down, repeatedly relocates it to the moving pad, and sends route keys during the hold; this is implementation evidence of the required visible control sequence.

Direction buttons remain effective while holding, and the static vehicle changes only on their clicks. Waiting therefore loses no action opportunity caused by task-state evolution, so no legitimate D, Delta, and w satisfies clause iii.
